archetypes.name: ledger-schema
archetypes.rationale: The plan depends on a new fixed-width timing-ledger row kind and JSON interval attachment, so schema drift would silently drop data.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the proposed 13-column round row layout, validation rules, and timing-report parsing align with the existing ledger contract and row_ok behavior. Check that skill plus timestamp interval matching is sufficient for implement and design parent steps, including repeated design Step 3 intervals and missing parent marks. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: count-source
archetypes.rationale: Round timing is only useful if accepted, rejected, and oos counts are sourced from the same artifacts and heading schemas the repo already uses.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify the plan's proposed accepted, rejected, and oos count sources against the actual implement and design tally artifacts. Pay special attention to whether rejected plan-review findings use the correct heading pattern and whether counts are per-round or cumulative at the emission point. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: flush-chain
archetypes.rationale: The user requirement includes committed run logs, so the plan must prove the new data flows from emission through report generation to batch flush without new flush sites.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the proposed telemetry path from review loops through timing-ledger, timing-report JSON generation, refresh-run-logs, and the committed timing-report batch. Look for missing handoffs, assumptions about batch validation, or places where additive fields could be stripped before reaching run logs. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
